habitat: Solitary or in groups on open inland waters with reed beds. It swims, sometimes dives, and walks at the edges of reed beds, on the shoreline and sometimes further into marshland. It often stands on floating nest mounds.
summary: A very common resident. The only all-black waterbird with a white frontal shield and bill. The legs and the lobed feet are grey. The immature is ash-brown and has no white shield. The call is clukuk or crornk. The Kemp name Redknobbed Coot and the code VB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Common Moorhen has a red bill and white flank marks. Red-knobbed Coot has a white bill and frontal shield and no white flank line.

viewNotes.note: All black, with a white bill and frontal shield. The feet are lobed and grey.
A flight pattern was not described.

calls.description: The normal call is clukuk or crornk. Grade A call from near Grahamstown, Eastern Cape. The filename says the file was edited. The filename is XC649289-Red-knobbed Coot exc edited.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a very common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The description says the shield and bill are white. It does not describe the colour of the knobs. The Kruger photograph is distant. The grade A call is from the Eastern Cape and the filename says it was edited. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.
